rollouts: 200 untrained-student rollouts, DAPO-Math-17k (en), the Phase 0 gate set

interpretation.headline: The lexical masks capture disproportionately LITTLE gradient mass, not disproportionately much. Every variant has a mass/token ratio below 1 (v0 0.546, v1 0.505, v0ms 0.535, v2 0.414): v0 spends 63.8% of the token budget to capture 34.8% of the divergence the trainer reduces.
interpretation.random_beats_them: A budget-matched random mask captures 54.7% (ratio 0.858) against v0's 34.8%. Since random-stratified reproduces v0's own positional profile, the gap is not positional -- within the same positions, the lexical criterion actively selects lower-mass tokens.
interpretation.why: Digits and operators inside LaTeX are among the most predictable tokens in a derivation. Once the student has emitted `\\frac{1}{`, the `2}` is nearly determined, teacher and student agree, and the divergence is small. The mass sits in the reasoning prose where the two models actually disagree.
interpretation.not_an_entropy_proxy: Jaccard overlap with budget-matched entropy top-k is only 0.28-0.32 (v2: 0.11), so the lexical masks are not a zero-cost approximation of entropy selection. They select something genuinely different -- which turns out to be the low-divergence half.
interpretation.dear_comparability: DEAR's quoted 39.1% (entropy) and 35.9% (random) are coverages at DEAR's budget, which is not stated here, so they cannot be compared to our coverages directly. The budget-independent quantity is the mass/token ratio; ours are entropy 1.477 and random 0.858. Report ratios, or re-measure at DEAR's budget.
interpretation.consequence: This is a pre-registered prediction for Phase 3 rather than a post-hoc excuse: if v0 trains on the tokens the teacher and student already agree on, it should underperform vanilla and its budget-matched random control. A null or negative accuracy result would then be mechanistically explained rather than merely observed.
